rows.speaker: ابن كثير، ابن محيصن، حميد، مجاهد، أبو عمرو، يعقوب، ابن وثاب، الأعمش، الكسائي
rows.claim: These readers pronounce yunazzilu without gemination; the remaining readers use the doubled form.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن وحميد ومجاهد وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وابن وثاب والأعمش وغيرهما والكسائي «ينزل» مخففا

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the verb with gemination.
rows.anchor: الباقون بالتشديد. وقرأ ابن وثاب أيضا والأعمش وغيرهما

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب، الأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab, al-Aʿmash, and others also read qanatū with kasra on the nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب أيضا والأعمش وغيرهما «قنطوا» بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayth means rain and is so named because it comes to the aid of creatures; the verb also describes rain reaching land or God giving rain to a country.
rows.anchor: والغيث المطر وسمي الغيث غيثا لأنه يغيث الخلق. وقد غاث الغيث الأرض أي أصابها

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī recounts an Arab woman answering that they were rained upon as much as they wished; al-Thaʿlabī transmits this first anecdote.
rows.anchor: وعن الأصمعي قال: مررت ببعض قبائل العرب وقد مطروا فسألت عجوزا منهم: أتاكم المطر؟ فقالت: غثنا ما شئنا غيثا

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma praises a woman’s eloquent use of “ghithnā”; al-Jawharī transmits this second anecdote.
rows.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة: قاتل الله أمة بني فلان ما أفصحها قلت لها كيف كان المطر عندكم؟ فقالت: غثنا ما شئنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds and vegetation may also be called ghayth.
rows.anchor: وربما سمى السحاب والنبات غيثا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qunūṭ means despair, as Qatāda and others explain.
rows.anchor: والقنوط الإياس قاله قتادة وغيره

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda reports that a man told ʿUmar people despaired amid drought; ʿUmar replied that rain would come, God willing, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ذكر أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب: يا أمير المؤمنين، قحط المطر وقل الغيث

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī distinguishes ghayth, beneficial rain in its proper season, from rain, which can benefit or harm in season or out of season.
rows.anchor: والغيث ما كان نافعا في وقته، والمطر قد يكون نافعا وضارا في وقته وغير وقته قاله الماوردي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets God’s spreading mercy as the rain itself.
rows.anchor: { وينشر رحمته } قيل المطر وهو قول السدي

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī gives another interpretation: the sun appearing after rain.
rows.anchor: وقيل ظهور الشمس بعد المطر ذكره المهدوي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed after rain was withheld from Mecca’s people for seven years, until they despaired and God sent rain.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: نزلت في حبس المطر عن أهل مكة سبع سنين حتى قنطوا، ثم أنزل الله المطر

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī offers the occasion of a Bedouin asking the Prophet about rain on Friday, in the report of the rain prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في الأعرابي سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المطر يوم الجمعة في خبر الاستسقاء ذكره القشيري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Walī is the one who supports His friends, and al-Ḥamīd is the One praised by every tongue.
rows.anchor: «الولي» الذي ينصر أولياءه. «الحميد» المحمود بكل لسان

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī glosses the phrase as Pharaoh making his people foolish; they obeyed because their minds were light and their reason limited.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: المعنى فاستجهل قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb can mean that joy unsettles someone or that someone induces another to act foolishly; the related verse warns against being unsettled by unbelievers.
rows.anchor: يقال: استخفه الفرح أي أزعجه، واستخفه أي حمله على الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that Pharaoh provoked his people with speech, and they obeyed him by accepting disbelief.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استفزهم بالقول فأطاعوه على التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says he found them intellectually weak; this alone cannot explain their obedience, so an unstated step must be supplied: he called them to error and they obeyed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استخف قومه أي وجدهم خفاف العقول. وهذا لا يدل على أنه يجب أن يطيعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as Pharaoh overpowering his people until they followed him; استخف به means to insult someone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: استخف قومه وقهرهم حتى اتبعوه يقال: استخفه خلاف استثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were a people who had departed from obedience to God.
rows.anchor: { إنهم كانوا قوما فاسقين } أي خارجين عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command “Take him” is addressed to the keepers of Hell and refers to the sinner.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { خذوه } أي يقال للزبانية خذوه يعني الأثيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtilūhu means drag and drive him; ʿatl is seizing a man by the lapels and pulling him violently toward imprisonment or calamity.
rows.anchor: والعتل: أن تأخذ بتلابيب الرجل فتعتله، أي تجره إليك لتذهب به إلى حبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb denotes violent pulling; a cited horse poem uses its lām form.
rows.anchor: عتلت الرجل أعتله وأعتله عتلا إذا جذبته جذبا عنيفا. ورجل معتل بالكسر

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt reports two forms, ʿatala and ʿatana, with lām and nūn.
rows.anchor: وفيه لغتان عتله وعتنه باللام والنون جميعا، قاله ابن السكيت

rows.speaker: الكوفيون، أبو عمرو
rows.claim: The Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read iʿtilūhu with kasra; the remaining readers use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون وأبو عمرو «فاعتلوه» بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawāʾ al-jaḥīm means the middle of Hell.
rows.anchor: { إلى سواء الجحيم } وسط الجحيم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil describes Mālik striking Abū Jahl’s head with an iron mace, splitting it so his brain runs down his body, then pouring intensely boiling water into him until it reaches his belly; the angel tells him to taste punishment.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يضرب مالك خازن النار ضربة على رأس أبي جهل بمقمع من حديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pouring of boiling water over their heads is compared with the description in 22:19.
rows.anchor: ونظيره: يصب من فوق رءوسهم الحميم [الحج:19]

rows.speaker: العوام، الحسن عن علي، الكسائي
rows.claim: The common readers agree on kasra in inna; al-Ḥasan reports from ʿAlī a reading with fatḥa, which al-Kisāʾī also read.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: أجمعت العوام على كسر «إن». وروي عن الحسن عن علي رحمه الله «ذق أنك» بفتح «أن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra one pauses after “taste”; with fatḥa one does not pause, since the sense is “taste because you are the mighty and noble one.”
rows.anchor: فمن كسر «إن» وقف على «ذق». ومن فتحها لم يقف على «ذق» لأن المعنى ذق لأنك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says it concerns Abū Jahl, who had claimed that no one in the region was more powerful or honored than he; the verse taunts him with his own boast.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: نزلت في أبي جهل وكان قد قال: ما فيها أعز مني ولا أكرم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: ʿIkrima recounts the Prophet warning Abū Jahl that God ordered him to say “woe to you”; Abū Jahl boasted of his power and honor, was killed and humiliated at Badr, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor:
وقال عكرمة:
" التقى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angel says this mockingly, according to Abū Jahl’s own claim that he was the mightiest and most honored in the valley.
rows.anchor: أي يقول له الملك: ذق إنك أنت العزيز الكريم بزعمك

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads the line as scorn, rebuke, mockery, insult, and degradation: it means “you are the lowly, humiliated one.”
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt is compared with the people of Shuʿayb calling him “the forbearing, right-minded one,” which one interpretation takes to mean foolish and ignorant.
rows.anchor: وهو كما قال قوم شعيب لشعيب: إنك لأنت الحليم الرشيد

words: إِنَّ هَٰذَا مَا كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَمْتَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels tell them that this is what they used to doubt in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أي تقول لهم الملائكة: إن هذا ما كنتم تشكون فيه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil identify the listeners as hypocrites, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy, Rifāʿa ibn al-Tābūt, Zayd ibn al-Ṣalt, al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr, and Mālik ibn Dukhshum; they attended Friday sermons, ignored mention of hypocrites, then asked about it afterward.
rows.anchor: كانوا يحضرون الخطبة يوم الجمعة فإذا سمعوا ذكر المنافقين فيها أعرضوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says they listened to the Prophet among the believers, but believers retained and understood his words while unbelievers did not.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يحضرون عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مع المؤمنين فيستمعون منه ما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means when they left or parted from the Prophet’s gathering.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا خرجوا من عندك } أي إذا فارقوا مجلسك

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima identifies those given knowledge as ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās; Ibn ʿAbbās says he was among those questioned and thus among the learned.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة: هو عبد الله بن العباس. قال ابن عباس: كنت ممن يسأل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عبد الله بن بريدة
rows.claim: Another transmission from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Burayda identifies the learned person as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية عن ابن عباس: أنه يريد عبد الله بن مسعود. وكذا قال عبد الله بن بريدة

rows.speaker: القاسم بن عبد الرحمن، ابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān identifies the learned person as Abū al-Dardāʾ; Ibn Zayd says the phrase refers to the Companions collectively.
rows.anchor: وقال القاسم بن عبد الرحمن: هو أبو الدرداء. وقال ابن زيد: إنهم الصحابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask “what did he just say?” mockingly, as though they had paid no attention; ānifan denotes the time nearest to the present, from beginning something anew.
rows.anchor: ماذا قال آنفا } أي الآن على جهة الاستهزاء. أي أنا لم ألتفت إلى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anf can mean the beginning: fresh pasture or an unused cup; anonymous poems illustrate that sense.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ويحرم سر جارتهم عليهم
ويأكل جارهم أنف القصاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poem uses anf for an unused cup; Imruʾ al-Qays uses the term for the beginning of a journey, and the nose of anything is its beginning.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: إن الشواء والنشيل والرغف والقينة الحسناء والكأس الأنف

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses anf for the beginning, as in “he carried me in his beginning.”
rows.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس: قد غدا يحملني في أنفه أي في أوله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda contrasts someone who understands God’s message and benefits from hearing it with someone who neither understands nor benefits; another saying divides listeners into acting, understanding, and heedlessly abandoning hearers.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في هؤلاء المنافقين: الناس رجلان: رجل عقل عن الله فانتفع بما سمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sealed their hearts, so they did not believe.
rows.anchor: { أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم } فلم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They followed their desires in disbelief.
rows.anchor: { واتبعوا أهواءهم } في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those guided are those guided to faith.
rows.anchor: { والذين اهتدوا } أي للإيمان زادهم الله هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says God increased their guidance.
rows.anchor: زادهم الله هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the Prophet increased their guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: زادهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the Qurʾān they heard was guidance that multiplied their certainty.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ما يستمعونه من القرآن هدى أي يتضاعف يقينهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the hypocrites’ turning away and mockery itself increased the believers’ guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: زادهم إعراض المنافقين واستهزاؤهم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the descent of abrogating revelation increased their guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: زادهم نزول الناسخ هدى

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Of four explanations for increased guidance, al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas says it means increased knowledge.
rows.anchor: أحدها زادهم علما قاله الربيع بن أنس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says they understood what they heard and acted on what they knew.
rows.anchor: الثاني أنهم علموا ما سمعوا وعملوا بما علموا قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says their guidance was greater insight into their religion and affirmation of their Prophet.
rows.anchor: الثالث زادهم بصيرة في دينهم وتصديقا لنبيهم قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth explanation is that God opened their breasts to the faith they already held.
rows.anchor: الرابع شرح صدورهم بما هم عليه من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that God inspired them with their piety.
rows.anchor: { وآتاهم تقواهم } أي ألهمهم إياها

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ interprets the piety given to them as fear of God.
rows.anchor: أحدها آتاهم الخشية قاله الربيع

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says it means the reward for their piety in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: الثاني ثواب تقواهم في الآخرة قاله السدي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil interprets it as God enabling them to perform what He obligated.
rows.anchor: الثالث وفقهم للعمل الذي فرض عليهم قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: ابن زياد، السدي
rows.claim: Ibn Ziyād and al-Suddī say God showed them what they should avoid.
rows.anchor: الرابع بين لهم ما يتقون قاله ابن زياد والسدي أيضا

rows.speaker: عطية
rows.claim: ʿAṭiyya says it means leaving the abrogated ruling and acting by the abrogating one.
rows.anchor: الخامس أنه ترك المنسوخ والعمل بالناسخ قاله عطية

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī adds a sixth possibility: leaving dispensations and choosing the stricter obligations.
rows.anchor: الماوردي: ويحتمل. سادسا أنه ترك الرخص والأخذ بالعزائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reading uses aʿṭāhum (“gave them”) instead of ātāhum.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «وأعطاهم» بدل «وآتاهم»

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says this passage was revealed concerning those among the People of the Book who believed.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: هذه نزلت فيمن آمن من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A male and a female” means Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: يعني آدم وحواء

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī says the verse was revealed specifically about Abū Hind: the Prophet ordered Banū Bayāḍa to marry him to a woman of their group, and they objected to marrying daughters to clients; Abū Dāwūd records the report in al-Marāsīl.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري: نزلت في أبي هند خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another occasion says the verse concerned Thābit ibn Qays, who insulted a man not making room by calling him the son of a woman; the Prophet said no one excels others except through piety.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنها نزلت في ثابت بن قيس بن شماس. وقوله في الرجل الذي لم يتفسح له

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In the Thābit report, the Prophet says no one excels others except through piety; 58:11 was revealed about the man who was not given room.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:«انظر في وجوه القوم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at the conquest of Mecca Bilāl called the prayer from the Kaʿba; ʿAttāb, al-Ḥārith, and Suhayl disparaged him, while Abū Sufyān feared God would inform the Prophet; Gabriel did so, the men admitted their remarks, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بلالا حتى علا على ظهر الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes boasting in ancestry, competing in wealth, and looking down on the poor: the criterion is piety, since everyone descends from Adam and Eve.
rows.anchor: زجرهم عن التفاخر بالأنساب، والتكاثر بالأموال، والازدراء بالفقراء

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying God removed jāhiliyya arrogance over ancestors: people are either righteous and honored by God or wicked and lowly; all descend from Adam, whom God created from dust.
rows.anchor: يأيها الناس إن الله قد أذهب عنكم عيبة الجاهلية وتعاظمها بآبائها

rows.speaker: يحيى بن معين
rows.claim: The preceding Ibn ʿUmar report is transmitted through ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar, father of ʿAlī ibn al-Madīnī; Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn and others graded it weak.
rows.anchor: خرجه من حديث عبد الله بن جعفر والد علي بن المديني وهو ضعيف، ضعفه يحيى بن معين وغيره

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Abū Naḍra the Prophet’s sermon at Minā during the middle days of Tashrīq: one Lord and father, no Arab/non-Arab or color group excels another except by piety, and witnesses should tell those absent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي نضرة قال: حدثني أو حدثنا من شهد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Abū Mālik al-Ashʿarī reports that God looks at hearts rather than status, ancestry, bodies, or wealth; all are Adam’s children, and the most pious are dearest to God.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن أبي مالك الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A poem attributed to ʿAlī says humans are equal through Adam and Eve, clay and water confer no honor, and worth lies in knowledge, guidance, and what a person does well rather than ignorance or ancestry.
rows.anchor: ولعلي رضي الله عنه في هذا المعنى وهو مشهور من شعره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creation from male and female is also stated at the beginning of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ; God could have created without a pair, as Adam, without a male, as Jesus, or without a female, as Eve.
rows.anchor: وكذلك في أول سورة «النساء». ولو شاء لخلقه دونهما كخلقه لآدم

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī notes that Eve was created from Adam’s rib, perhaps representing creation from one parent alone; divine power to create in other ways did not make those possibilities actual.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء أن آدم خلق الله منه حواء من ضلع انتزعها من أضلاعه فلعله هذا القسم قاله ابن العربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made people into lineages, in-law relations, tribes, and peoples so that they could recognize and connect with one another, according to His determined wisdom.
rows.anchor: خلق الله الخلق بين الذكر والأنثى أنسابا وأصهارا وقبائل وشعوبا، وخلق لهم منها التعارف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying someone’s actual lineage can incur the legal penalty for slander, including falsely calling an Arab non-Arab or vice versa.
rows.anchor: فإذا نفاه رجل عنه استوجب الحد بقذفه مثل أن ينفيه عن رهطه وحسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An earlier view held that a fetus comes only from the man’s fluid; the preceding quotations are cited to argue creation comes from a single fluid.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن الخلق من ماء واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correct view is that human creation comes from both the man’s and woman’s fluids, because this verse states it explicitly and cannot bear an alternative interpretation.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن الخلق إنما يكون من ماء الرجل والمرأة لهذه الآية فإنها نص لا يحتمل التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fluid described as emerging from between the backbone and ribs refers to men’s backbones and women’s ribs, as will be explained later.
rows.anchor: والمراد منه أصلاب الرجال وترائب النساء على ما يأتي بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses mention water, a fluid, and a drop without assigning them exclusively to either parent; this supports shared parentage, since women emit fluid like men and resemblance derives from both.
rows.anchor: فليس فيه أكثر من أن الله تعالى ذكر خلق الإنسان من الماء والسلالة والنطفة ولم يضفها إلى أحد الأبوين دون الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s flood involved rainwater and the earth’s water, since meeting requires two sources; similarly, “a fluid” may mean fluids from both parents.
rows.anchor: وإنما أراد ماء السماء وماء الأرض لأن الالتقاء لا يكون إلا من اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation makes shuʿūb the heads of major groupings such as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, Aws, and Khazraj; the singular is shaʿb, named for branching and gathering like tree limbs.
rows.anchor: الشعوب رؤوس القبائل مثل ربيعة ومضر والأوس والخزرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root can mean either gathering or separating: a mishʿab needle joins, while death is called shuʿūb because it separates.
rows.anchor: والشعب من الأضداد يقال شعبته إذا جمعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, shaʿb means a mountain path, plural shiʿāb; al-Jawharī says shaʿb also denotes what branches from Arab or non-Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: فأما الشعب بالكسر فهو الطريق في الجبل والجمع الشعاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shuʿūbiyya is a group that does not rank Arabs above non-Arabs; in a hadith, a man from the shuʿūb means a non-Arab.
rows.anchor: والشعوبية: فرقة لا تفضل العرب على العجم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a shaʿb is the great tribe that gathers its branches, such as Muḍar, while qabāʾil are its subdivisions.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الشعوب الجمهور مثل مضر. والقبائل الأفخاذ

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One report from Mujāhid says shuʿūb are more distant lineages and qabāʾil nearer ones.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الشعوب البعيد من النسب والقبائل دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also means to separate; death is called shuʿūb because it divides people.
rows.anchor: وشعبته إذا فرقته، ومنه سميت المنية شعوبا لأنها مفرقة

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawharī says shaʿb is what branches from Arab or non-Arab tribes, with shuʿūb as its plural.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: الشعب: ما تشعب من قبائل العرب والعجم والجمع الشعوب

rows.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: A second report from Mujāhid, also attributed to Qatāda, reverses the distinction: shuʿūb are nearer lineages; al-Māwardī transmits this version.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا أن الشعوب النسب الأقرب. وقاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poet says he saw many lineages but none like Saʿd ibn Mālik; another poem says that many tribal groups contain no noble or distinguished person.
rows.anchor: رأيت سعودا من شعوب كثيرة فلم أر سعدا مثل سعد بن مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify shuʿūb as Yemen’s Qaḥṭān and qabāʾil as Rabīʿa, Muḍar, and other ʿAdnān tribes, or as non-Arab subgroups versus Arab ones.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الشعوب عرب اليمن من قحطان، والقبائل من ربيعة ومضر وسائر عدنان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbās makes shuʿūb the clients and qabāʾil the Arabs; al-Qushayrī specifies peoples without known ancestry, such as Indians, mountaineers, and Turks.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية: إن الشعوب الموالي، والقبائل العرب

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī suggests shuʿūb may refer to people associated with regions and routes, while qabāʾil share common ancestry.
rows.anchor: الماوردي: ويحتمل أن الشعوب هم المضافون إلى النواحي والشعاب

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد، ابن الكلبي
rows.claim: One hierarchy ranks shaʿb above qabila, faṣīla, ʿimāra, baṭn, and fakhdh; another adds ʿashīra after faṣīla.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عبيد عن ابن الكلبي عن أبيه: الشعب أكبر من القبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another ordering is shaʿb, qabila, ʿimāra, baṭn, fakhdh, faṣīla, then ʿashīra; poets give mnemonic lists.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الشعب ثم القبيلة ثم العمارة ثم البطن ثم الفخذ ثم الفصيلة ثم العشيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet gives shaʿb, qabila, ʿimāra, baṭn, then fakhdh, adding that a youth is sheltered only by his faṣīla.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر: قبيلة قبلها شعب وبعدهما عمارة ثم بطن تلوه فخذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse reiterates the point made at 43:44: God and His Messenger regard piety, not ancestry, as the criterion.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في سورة «الزخرف» عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with fatḥa on an is explained as answering why people should not boast of ancestry: the most honored before God is the most pious, not the best connected.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل: لم يتفاخر بالأنساب؟ قيل: لأن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhī reports from Samura that the Prophet said status comes from wealth but nobility from piety; he grades the report ḥasan gharīb ṣaḥīḥ.
rows.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن سمرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever wishes to be the most honored of people should fear God.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء منصوصا عنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwā means observing God’s boundaries in commands and prohibitions, embodying what He ordered and avoiding what He forbade.
rows.anchor: والتقوى معناه مراعاة حدود الله تعالى أمرا ونهيا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra quotes God saying He made lineage and made piety the criterion of honor, while people insisted on boasting about ancestors; on Judgment Day God will raise His own lineage and lower theirs, calling for the pious.
rows.anchor: وفي الخبر من رواية أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet’s allies on Judgment Day are the pious, even if another person has closer lineage; people bring deeds while others carry worldly goods and appeal to him.
rows.anchor: وروى الطبري من حديث أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr reports the Prophet publicly saying that his father’s family are not his allies; his ally is God and the righteous believers.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: من أكرم الناس؟

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet first naming Joseph, son of Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham as most honored, then teaching that the most honored before God is the most pious; the best Arabs in pre-Islamic times are best in Islam if they understand religion.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: من أكرم الناس؟ فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem says wealth is no source of honor, all honor belongs to the pious, and someone who knows God but gains no benefit from that knowledge is wretched.
rows.anchor: وأنشدوا في ذلك: ما يصنع العبد بعز الغنى والعز كل العز للمتقي

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd that an Anṣārī man defended marrying for religion and character after his wife’s lineage was criticized; the Prophet said Islam lifted low status and removed blame, now belonging only to jāhiliyya.
rows.anchor: ذكر الطبري حدثني عمر بن محمد قال حدثنا عبيد بن إسحاق العطار

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says he hopes to be the most God-fearing and most knowledgeable about what to avoid; al-Qurṭubī concludes that this makes him the noblest of people before God.
rows.anchor:
وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إني لأرجو أن أكون أخشاكم لله

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says this is the principle Mālik considered in marriage compatibility.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهذا الذي لحظ مالك في الكفاءة في النكاح

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: According to ʿAbd Allāh’s transmission from Mālik, a client may marry an Arab woman, based on this verse.
rows.anchor: روى عبد الله عن مالك: يتزوج المولى العربية

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة، الشافعي
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī take lineage and wealth into account in marriage compatibility.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والشافعي: يراعي الحسب والمال

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: In a report in the Ṣaḥīḥ, ʿĀʾisha recounts that Abū Ḥudhayfa adopted Sālim and married him to his niece Hind bint al-Walīd; Sālim was a client of an Anṣārī woman.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح عن عائشة أن أبا حذيفة بن عتبة بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further examples are Ḍubāʿa bint al-Zubayr married to al-Miqdād, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf’s sister to Bilāl, and Zaynab bint Jaḥsh to Zayd ibn Ḥāritha.
rows.anchor: وضباعة بنت الزبير كانت تحت المقداد بن الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These examples establish that clients may marry Arab women and that compatibility is based on religion.
rows.anchor: فدل على جواز نكاح الموالي العربية، وإنما تراعى الكفاءة في الدين

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī, Sahl ibn Saʿd reports the Prophet asking about a well-regarded man and then a poor Muslim; people deem the latter unsuitable, but the Prophet says he is better than the whole earth filled with the first man’s like.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه أيضا ما روى سهل بن سعد في صحيح البخاري

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says a woman is married for wealth, beauty, religion, and in a variant lineage, then advises choosing the religious woman.
rows.anchor:
وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" تنكح المرأة لمالها وجمالها ودينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salmān proposed to Abū Bakr’s daughter and was accepted; ʿUmar declined his proposal, and when ʿUmar later asked Salmān to marry her, Salmān refused.
rows.anchor: وقد خطب سلمان إلى أبي بكر ابنته فأجابه

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: When Banū al-Bukayr refused Bilāl’s proposal, he complained to the Prophet, who became angry on his behalf; the brothers then married their sister to him.
rows.anchor: وخطب بلال بنت البكير فأبى إخوتها، فقال بلال: يا رسول الله، ماذا لقيت

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī introduces the Prophet’s statement about Abū Hind, who cupped him; the quotation continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في أبي هند حين حجمه

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet urged people to marry Abū Hind and marry into his family; Abū Hind was a client of Banū Bayāḍa.
rows.anchor: " أنكحوا أبا هند وأنكحوا إليه " وهو مولى بني بياضة

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī reports from ʿĀʾisha that Abū Hind, who cupped the Prophet, was praised as someone whose heart God had filled with faith, followed by the Prophet’s marriage encouragement.
rows.anchor: وروى الدارقطني من حديث الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة أن أبا هند مولى بني بياضة

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī says lineage may count in compatibility when it means connection to the Prophet’s family, scholars, or notable ascetics and righteous people; a pious believer outranks a wicked noble, but among equally pious people lineage can prevail, as youth over age in prayer when piety is equal.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري أبو نصر: وقد يعتبر النسب في الكفاءة في النكاح وهو الاتصال بشجرة النبوة
